This was followed by Basa Chilly, something that wasn't on the menu but prepared upon our request, and it turned out to be simply fantastic. For the main course, we opted for a **Pizza Quattro Staggioni and **Pesto Gnocchi**.

The **Pesto Gnocchi**, on the other hand, was the real standout—pillowy-soft gnocchi coated in a fragrant, flavorful pesto sauce that wasn’t too overpowering. reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"anil sharma\",\"time_line\":\"4 months ago\",\"review\":\"Oye Kake is a vegetarian Punjabi restaurant located on Patel Street in Fort, Mumbai. It is close to famous places like CST and the Gateway of India. The restaurant has a bright and colorful look with Punjabi-style decoration. The walls have fun paintings, and the furniture gives a dhaba (roadside eatery) feel.\\n\\nThe food here is tasty and made with good ingredients. The Amritsari Kulcha Thali is one of the best items. It comes with stuffed kulcha, spicy chole (chickpeas), salad, and curd. The kulcha is soft from inside and crispy outside. The chole is full of flavor. The Dal Makhani is creamy and rich, perfect with butter naan. The Paneer Bhurji and Rajma Chawal also taste like home-cooked food.\\n\\nThe sweet lassi and mango lassi are served in large glasses and are thick and fresh. They go well with the food and are very filling.\\n\\nPrices are a bit high, but the quality and taste make it worth it, especially for special occasions or weekend lunch. Portion size is good, but not very big.\\n\\nThe staff is friendly and gives fast service. The place is clean, including the washroom. During busy hours, you might have to wait a little, but not too long.\\n\\nOye Kake is a good choice if you are looking for pure vegetarian Punjabi food in South Mumbai. ["{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Been here few days back for lunch. This restaurant is cited inside a 4 star property i.e Ramee Guestline Dadar.

Rasoi kitchen and bar is all about the experience and top notch f&b.
The entire restaurant is well designed which has this really nice and calming Atmosphere and it looks fab. Loved the decor a lot as there are few elements which looks quirky and premium.

So we had a couple of drinks and food dishes over here and we loved every single thing.
For drinks we ordered for Anar ka pyar which was mix of pomegranate, cranberry and lime juice. Loved it! Also from the mango special menu we tried Mango Colada which was hands down the best one in my opinion and we would strongly recommend trying this one.

For Starters they have a lot to choose from. We ordered Prawns sukka which was this semi thick gravy having the dominant flavor of Coconut and home ground spices. Fabulous!
Also had Murgh Multani Tikka which was by far one of the best kebab we have tasted. First up the portion served was twice what we get anywhere. Loved the plating too!

Later for the main course we had Prawns Goan curry which was scrumptious and had perfect consistency. 5 pieces of decent sized prawns into that luscious gravy paired with naan was true bliss. Last up we had Thai curry which was served with steamed rice and it had a good amount of veggies and chicken in it. Totally value for money and incredible taste as well.

Desserts are always my favourite part of the meal and rasoi made sure we had a great ending for this yummy meal. In house Kulfi Falooda was our call and right from the presentation to taste it was lovely. If you are someone who loves falooda then this one for you.

Rasoi kitchen & Bar offers really nice service as well. The staff is well trained and they are quite attentive too. Would be visiting here again with my family., name_person=V&S}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=As I entered Rasoi, I was greeted by a warm and inviting ambiance with elegant decor and comfortable seating. The attentive staff promptly escorted me to my table, and I was eager to explore the menu. I started my culinary journey with their Mocktail Caribbean Delight, a refreshing blend of tropical fruit flavors with a hint of mint, which was a perfect start to my meal. My companion opted for the cocktail New York Sour, a classic whiskey-based cocktail with a tangy twist of lemon, which was a perfect balance of sweet and sour notes.

For appetizers, we tried the Murg Mastani Tikka and Bhatti da Murg. The Murg Mastani Tikka was a succulent and flavorful chicken tikka marinated with aromatic spices, while the Bhatti da Murg was a juicy and tender tandoori chicken with a smoky flavor that left us craving for more. The combination of the two appetizers was a perfect blend of traditional and contemporary flavors, and we thoroughly enjoyed them.

Moving on to the main course, we opted for the Nawabi Murg with Cheese Garlic Naan and Nukkad Wali Biryani. The Nawabi Murg was a rich and creamy chicken curry with a velvety gravy that was packed with flavors. The chicken was cooked to perfection, and the dish was a perfect balance of spices and creaminess. The Cheese Garlic Naan was a heavenly combination of gooey cheese and aromatic garlic, which complemented the curry perfectly. The Nukkad Wali Biryani was a fragrant and flavorful rice dish with tender pieces of meat and aromatic spices that were a treat to the taste buds.

To end our culinary journey on a sweet note, we indulged in the Kulfi Falooda, a classic Indian dessert with a twist. The creamy and rich kulfi was served with a generous topping of vermicelli and rose syrup, which added a burst of flavors to the dessert. It was a delightful combination of textures and flavors that left us craving for more.

The service at Rasoi was impeccable, with attentive staff who were knowledgeable about the menu and provided prompt service throughout our meal. I recently dined at Hotel Grand Central in Chembur and had a mixed experience. The first thing that stands out about this restaurant is its inviting ambience. The decor is tasteful, creating a cozy and comfortable atmosphere that makes you feel at ease as soon as you step in.

However, while the ambience is impressive, the food was just okay. The dishes were decent but didn't quite live up to my expectations in terms of flavor. That said, the variety on the menu is good, so there’s plenty to choose from.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Valet, E:PARKING_OPTION_VALET], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Masque was very good, but just shy of being amazing. Would rate this 3.5/5.

The food was consistently good, but not great. Everything was beautifully made, perfectly presented but the taste of everything left us feeling a bit lacking. Or as my wife said, it missed “ooomph”. After having spent the last few weeks at other restaurants like the Bombay Canteen, Papa’s, O’Pedro etc, the food at Masque felt like the bottom of this group. It is actually surprising how it was ranked number 2 on the top 50 restaurants list. Not saying the food is bad, not by any means. It is really good, but not worthy of being number 2.

The service was good, but staff can be better trained to be more cohesive, quiet and smooth. This could be a high standard having spent time experiencing the world class service at Papa’s.

The atmosphere was simplistic, slightly modern and feels cold. It’s not a warm and cozy atmosphere, it’s slightly more formal. The bar occasionally gets very very loud with the sound of ice shaking but other than that, it’s quite comfortable. Staff is attentive and happy to help.

We did really like the experience of them bringing us into the kitchen for the first course, but again, kind of felt like a gimmick. This can be done better.

The bill for 6 of us with a few drinks came to about 60,000. For this price, the quality and taste of the food was not worth it. We felt quite disappointed, specially considering the reputation, reviews and ranking that Masque has.

There are other restaurants of much higher calibre. If you want to spend similar money and are fortunate enough to get a table, go to Papa’s.

For a slightly more accessible experience, go to Bombay Canteen.

We’re glad we tried this, it was a unique experience, but probably won’t return unless there’s a completely new menu., name_person=Nirav Tanna}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=From start to finish, this was one of the best tasting menu experiences I’ve ever had. We were invited into the chef’s kitchen at the start of the evening, where the team greeted us warmly and took a photo — a memorable way to kick things off.
Once seated, the magic really unfolded. The 10-course tasting menu came with no preview, which made each dish a fun and delicious surprise. Every plate was beautifully executed, creative, and perfectly paced.
The service was equally outstanding. The waiters were not just professional but incredibly knowledgeable about each dish, its ingredients, and the cooking techniques behind it. Their enthusiasm really elevated the experience.
A phenomenal meal and an even better overall experience. It was the first of four fine dining restaurants we tried in Mumbai, and it set the bar really high. The execution and flavor mastery of every dish was spot-on. The trip to the kitchen for a palate cleanser (and a Polaroid-style photo memory) was a fun surprise. When you find yourself in Mumbai, Masque is a must., name_person=Miro K}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=3 months ago, review=So we keep trying the set course menu at most of our special occasions and would rate  Masque as the 2nd best

Woukd rate Tresind over them but they surely outscore Indian Accent in terms of flavour and creativity and definitely much ahead of Ekaa., name_person=Ankush Manwati}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=Edited 6 months ago, review=The journey to Masque begins with a whatsapp interrogation regarding the prospective guest's dietary preferences, allergies and information that a Rs 5000 deposit for two guests is mandatory which will be set off against the final bill. Your preferred table booking time will be confirmed only if the appropriate answers are provided. After an analysis of your answers you  are accepted! BUT only if you are not late by more than 15 minutes of the appointed time. But if you are - all is lost - the food, the 5000 and your mood. There were multiple messages regarding being on time.
Once you arrive at the Masque - you see a black wall and a black door which opens to reveal the restaurant. If you are early you may choose your table. Once at the table, each seat has a cocktail (Rs 5500)and wine pairing (Rs 5500 to Rs 7700) lists. You will also get sheets of listing of mocktails (Rs 2250), progressive cocktail pairing (Rs. 7700). This is in addition to the 10 course tasting menu priced at Rs. 6500 per head.
The food is flavourful. Except for the main course, which was dosa and smoked pork or Koji Sunchoke the rest were small portions. The gelatos were very tiny. The dish preparations were interesting in the way thupka or ravioli were recreated. The pomfret/besara/trout roe and the lamb/rezala/confit duck were very nice.
We selected the progressive cocktail menu. The first drink was of gin (mountain goat) where there was no flavour of gin. The tequila and mezcal cocktails were good. Rosso made from bourbon was ok.
The staff knew the food well. But they kept changing and each had a different attitude. One of them was quite dismissive of some premium Indian wine we asked about which was not listed on the Masque wine menu.
Ritwik at the bar was a helpful staff member and enlivened the evening with his fliar behind the bar.
All in all an ok, ok experience., name_person=SS Gill}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Really really good cocktail program - the Mezcal pairings were great.

And for the past couple of years I’ve made it a ritual to go here with my friends every time we visit Mumbai.

Every visit I had here has been nothing short of a fantastic experience. From the excellent service by the waiters, the yummy taste of well-made Goan food to the fun vibe the place and it’s people exuberate, it’s become my goto place in Mumbai for a fun night of singing. Even the hosts of the karaoke are very gracious and friendly and made each of our visit a memorable one, thus urging me to drop a 5-star rating which this venue has earned. The soft amber lighting and warm wood accents mirror the hues of the season outside, creating an atmosphere that feels both elegant and inviting. Subtle notes of spice—cinnamon, nutmeg, perhaps even a whisper of roasted chestnut—float through the air, hinting at what the kitchen has prepared.
The special autumn menu is the star of the evening, a celebration of comfort elevated to luxury. Each dish arrives like a small story of the season: vibrant, warm, and thoughtfully composed.
The meal might begin with a velvety roasted pumpkin soup, poured tableside into a bowl dotted with toasted seeds and a swirl of infused cream. Its aroma alone feels like a warm wool scarf wrapped around your senses. Let's start with the positive. The atmosphere is undoubtedly appealing; it's a stylish, modern space with a nice vibe that makes a good first impression. This was complemented by genuinely good service. Our server was attentive, friendly, and efficient, ensuring our glasses were never empty and checking in on us at just the right times.

However, these positives were significantly overshadowed by the venue's major drawback: its size. The place is simply too small for the crowd it attracts. Tables are crammed uncomfortably close together, making private conversation nearly impossible and creating a constant, cramped feeling. The noise level was high, and navigating to the restroom felt like an obstacle course.

Unfortunately, the most disappointing aspect was the food, which I found to be below average. While presented nicely, my main course was underseasoned and lacked the freshness and flavour I expected for the price. It felt like a dish going through the motions without any passion or precision.

From the moment you walk in, the vibe feels modern, artistic, and full of curiosity - and a sense that you’re about to experience something different. This place is creativity plated beautifully.

We began with their mocktails, the Pineapple Burn Fizz and Coconut Water Margarita, both refreshing and thoughtfully crafted - ideal palate cleansers before diving into the food.

The starters were where Spice Klub really showed its innovation. The Green Goodness Kebab, a sesame-crusted vegetable kebab, was crisp on the outside and soft within, paired perfectly with tzatziki and chimichurri for a refreshing herby punch. The Vadapav Mousse was a complete surprise—in the best way possible. Vadapav reimagined as a creamy mousse, served with soft pav and bursts of chutney pearls, it was shockingly delicious. The Manchurian 2.0 was glazed in Indo-Asian flavours.

For mains, we tried the Paneer Lazeez, a smoky, spiced makhani-style gravy that felt rich yet well-balanced. The paneer was soft and flavorful, pairing beautifully with the garlic butter naan and butter rumali roti—classic comfort done with finesse.

Dessert was equally indulgent. The Sizzling Gajar Delight arrived on a hot plate with warm gajar halwa, creamy rabdi, and a kulfi, making it a perfect mix of temperatures, textures, and nostalgia.

Overall, Spice Klub is a must-visit for anyone who loves innovative, vegetarian North Indian cuisine. It’s creative without being gimmicky, rooted in tradition yet unapologetically modern. But despite the charming name and the promise of a thoughtfully curated Italian menu, the experience left more to be desired than remembered.

The meal started on a reasonably positive note. The Spaghetti Carbonara arrived with a creamy, well-emulsified sauce that clung nicely to the strands of pasta. The presence of pork gave the dish some much-needed body and savouriness, though it was hard to tell if guanciale was used. The overall flavour was pleasant, if unremarkable, and the dish did what it needed to without dazzling.

Unfortunately, the meal only declined from there.

The Steak, requested medium rare, did arrive at the correct doneness, which deserves acknowledgement. But that’s where the positives end. The cut of meat itself was a poor choice—tough, chewy, and devoid of the tenderness one expects from a properly sourced and rested steak. For a dish that typically commands a premium on any menu, this one felt more like an afterthought than a main event.

The Salmon Bruschetta fared no better. Topped with pallid, clearly farmed salmon that lacked freshness, the dish suffered from a lack of depth and definition. The cream which is meant to support or complement actually ended up dominating the plate. The result was a bland, vaguely fishy bite that could have come from any cold appetiser counter rather than a kitchen claiming Italian sophistication.

And therein lies the central issue with Napoli by Shatranj. While it gestures toward authenticity and finesse, the food rarely lands with the kind of precision or character that might distinguish it. The pricing, meanwhile, reflects a confidence that the food does not back up. At best, it feels like another stylish Bandra restaurant with a name borrowed from Naples but very little of its soul.

reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"vishal sawant\",\"time_line\":\"a month ago\",\"review\":\"I recently visited Farzi Caf\u00e9 at Oberoi Mall, and it was a delightful dining experience overall. So quietly went in for lunch on a weekday.\\nThe Restaurant was relatively empty with handful of customers.\\nTheir starters (Prawn and Chicken) both tasted really good, highlighted more by the presentation.\\nThe Biriyani was good too, but was a bit too spicy for my taste.\\nService was a bit slow.\\nHowever because of the food, I might still visit them once more!\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b91,800\u20132,000\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":4,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":4,\"GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION\":\"Walk-ins only\",\"GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL\":\"Quiet, easy to talk\",\"GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME\":\"No wait\",\"GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS\":\"Somewhat recommend\",\"GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO\":[\"Vegetarian_menu_or_section\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS\":[\"Vegetarian_options\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS\"]}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Suyash Karangutkar\",\"time_line\":\"5 months ago\",\"review\":\"Farzi Caf\u00e9 lived up to its reputation of blending Indian flavors with modern culinary imagination. Our recent visit was a delightful experience that hit the right notes, not just in taste but in atmosphere and service too.\\n\\nWe began our meal with the Sweet Corn Soup with Cornflakes Churan and Herbs. This was no ordinary corn soup\u2014it was comforting, delicately spiced, and full of character. The corn kernels added texture, while the cornflakes and herb seasoning gave the broth a refreshing twist, balanced perfectly with coriander. A warm, flavorful start that set the tone for the rest of the meal.\\n\\nNext came the Chicken Thukpa with Ramen Noodles, Chicken Dumpling, in Truffle Oil. This fusion take on the classic Himalayan dish was mellow yet richly flavored. The dumplings were tender, the noodles soaked in the mildly spiced broth, and the touch of truffle oil added a subtle umami depth. The half-boiled egg was a nice touch.\\n\\nThe Salli Boti Bao was a creative surprise\u2014soft, open bao buns filled with spicy, well-marinated mutton boti, drenched in a desi-style gravy and topped with crispy potato salli. A clever and satisfying bite with layers of flavor and texture.\\n\\nFor drinks, we tried the F.B., a self-proclaimed \u2018Farzified\u2019 bong-style cocktail. It was quite the mix\u2014vodka, gin, rum, peach pur\u00e9e, and cranberry juice, rounded off with a jelly syrup that gave it a playful sweetness.\\n\\nWe also sampled the Litchi Panna Desire, a refreshing blend of lychee, lime, and mango panna, which was equal parts tart and tropical.\\n\\nFor the main course, we went traditional with the Saag Paneer Tarkari, paired with Meethi Laccha Paratha. The saag, a hearty combination of spinach, mustard greens, chopped vegetables, and crisp-edged paneer cubes, was rich and earthy. The preparation was just okay—the skin wasn’t crispy, and the duck itself was on the smaller side but came from Thailand. On a positive note, the dim sum was quite good, and I was impressed by how they cater to a wide range of dietary preferences, with no lard used in their offerings. We also tried the stir-fried buffalo, which was surprisingly delicious—tender, not too gamey, and packed with flavor.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Having lived and worked in Japan, albeit many moons ago, I was not expecting to be reminded of the tastes and feel of a typical izakaya in the land of the rising sun, in, of all places, Bandra, Mumbai.
We were ushered to our seating by a raucous welcome from the Kuuraku staff, which was more reminiscent of the Wankhede Stadium than a Japanese restaurant. But there was a effervescence about the staff at Kuuraku, reflecting the confidence that they have in their excellent food.
We ordered the Special Kushi Course, comprising 5 sticks of yakitori. The standout of this was the chicken tail. It was so good that we ordered two extra sticks of this, named bonjiri shio. We also ordered a portion of pork belly yakitori although this was very slightly disappointing as it was a little on the tough side. Another slight disappointment was the chargrilled asparagus wrapped in pork belly. Again, the pork belly wasn't as tender as I expected and the asparagus was a little small and fibrous. However, the edamame challenge was a lot of fun. The idea is to grab as much edamame as possible with one hand - and what you grab is what you get to eat. I used my goalkeeper hands to grab, what the server told me was an over par amount. The edamame was quite good too. The crunchy ebi roll was very generous too coming as a generous portion. The temperature of the rice was spot on as was the consistency. Could the quality of the rice be higher as in Japan? Well yes if you can get that rice but otherwise it really was excellent. The same goes for the pork rice. Here the consistency or the stickiness of the rice was more important than in the ebi roll and if they could get better rice it was be amazing. The slight disappointment was the inclusion of bell peppers. Heresy! Finally, the tea was served in a beautiful black pot, again, very true to Japan.
All in all this was an excellent place with a really true feel of Japan, helped also by the constant stream of Japanese music and the service was particularly excellent. ["{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=Located near Citylight theater, Ram Punjab was renovated a couple of years ago to get a more upmarket feel, while still maintaining pocket friendly rates. I have been here many times for a snack or a drink but this time I dropped in for a proper meal so here goes. The ambience is not great, it's not what you would call a family friendly place, though nothing like a desi bar, and it does get noisy when crowded. We opened our innings with Smirnoff, and the first starter was Murg Koliwada. They're essentially chicken nuggets, crispy outer layer, delicious meat on the inside, I strongly recommend this one. Murg Sholey Kebab was our next starter, which is chicken kebabs covered in egg fluff. The fluff tastes good only when genuinely hot, so I suggest licking off that first, and then attacking the chicken which was very tender, a little on the sweeter side. With the vodka done we now had rum running down our throats in the form of the all time favourite Old Monk. For the mains we ordered Murg Patiala (what's with everything being named "Murg"!) with Butter Roti. The rotis have enough butter on them to give you a heart attack by just looking at them, but then that's also what makes them so pleasurable for the taste buds. Murg Patiala is chicken and gravy in an omelette, and I totally loved it, a must have in my opinion. Portions served are quite sizeable, so we were too stuffed to have any desserts. The only major downside to this place is the service, which can vary from average to disastrous. From the waiters not being attentive to totally lacking any etiquette, it can be both funny and frustrating. During this particular visit, we were given only forks along with the starters, so we asked for spoons. After a brief wait the waiter arrived and literally threw the spoons on the table!! Heading straight to what was on offer for Experience Thali - Veg

To begin with we were presented with a palate cleanser - Amuse Bouche. Crispy and Spiced Masala Chana Dal packed in edible plastic. I was intrigued about the ingredients used and technique to make this, but it stays as a secret with the restaurant and chef. Very unique and impressed I must say!

We started with Appetizers and were served three of them - Jaipuri Paneer Tikka, Bhune Subz Ki Shami and Sarson Brocolli Tandoori. Paneer Tikka was smoked cottage cheese marinated with olives. The olives gave it a bitter taste for me and I personally love the smokey effect given to cottage cheese. However in this process the cottage cheese might have become a little hard. Something, which can be looked into.

Next we had the Bhune Subz Ki Shami - Round shaped Patties / Tikkis with peas and spiced beans as filling, fried to perfection. Highly recommended to try! After this, we tried the Sarson Broccoli Tandoori - marinated with mustard and grilled to perfection! Loved it! Must try!

Before heading into the mains, we were served another palate cleanser - this time around it was Mango & Lemon Sorbet served in a cutting chai glass. Loved the combination and was very refreshing. Again very unique!

And now coming to the Star Veg Thali at Kebeb Korner - 5 Vegetables and 1 Dal with Assorted Indian Breads along with choice of steamed rice / Khichdi. The thali was presented in a beautiful way. They have a shiny steel arc where all the individual bowls are placed. So all of these 6 bowls along with a bowl of salad is placed in front of you at one go, unlike other thali places where different people serve you continuously which can be irritating at times.

The best part here at Kebab Korner is that you get a thali experience without any hassles. Coming to the 5 vegetables - Bhuna Gobi Masala, Paneer Butter Masala, Subz Miloni, Lehsooni Palak and Beawar Bhindi. Amongst the five my preference would be Beawar Bhindi, Bhuna Gobi Masala and Paneer Butter Masala. Crisp Bhindi (lady fingers) with perfect potli masalas and cherry tomato. Personally I am not a fan of Bhindi, but with the way it was made and tasted, loved it.

Bhuna Gobi Masala, chopped cauliflower tossed with Indian spices and Paneer Butter Masala -creamy cottage cheese in a rich onion and tomato gravy, both came a close second for me.

Dal in the thali was Kebab Korner Signature Dal Makhani. Creamy Black Lentils Dal to be enjoyed with Indian Assorted breads as well as with Steam rice. Tasted real nice. I also tried the Khichdi, could be a good light option after heavy meal.

Loved the dessert, must try and highly recommended! And towards the end we were presented with a platter of paan - Meetha (Sweet) and Saada (Plain). Couldnt have asked for more!

Overall, if I need to define my experience at Kebab Korner in one word, it will be awestruck! ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=a month ago, review=A 4.5 rating experience.

Agent Jack’s Bar is located on the 6th floor of Fun Republic Mall Andheri West.

The restaurant is spacious with nicely lit ceiling and minimal elements added to the ambiance. They have a small bar at the center, an elevated space for DJ and a space is also kept for live music. The seatings available provides option for all size of groups.

Their menu covers Indian, Chinese and Italian. Options available are great as the menu is compact and hence it doesn’t confuses you. Prices are at par with similar type of brands and the quantity served is decent.

We went here for a weekday dinner and there was live music which was excellent. The kitchen service was on time and table service by Staff Dipu was good as he was attentive.

What We Had-
APPETISERS~
Loaded Nachos -
Nachos topped with beans, salsa, cheese sauce and sour cream tasted decent as everything about the dish was perfect except the nachos as they lacked the freshness. So minor improvement needed here.

Madras Fusion Chicken -
Juicy chicken tossed in creamy coconut garlic based sauce tasted delicious. Loved the flavours in this as even this had coconut milk it wasn’t sweet and the chicken was tender.

Chicken Shole -
One of the best classic chicken tikka experiences as this dish tasted outstanding. Spice rub was really food, the grilling was perfect and the chutney onion served along was great.

MAINS~
Paneer Tikka Pizza -
Nicely done base topped with sauce, cheese and paneer tikka tasted good. It was a classic pizza done right.

Chicken Korean Rice -
Looked delicious and tasted exactly the same. Basic yet full marks for this as the rice done in Korean sauce along with egg and chicken tasted great.

DESSERT~
Chocolate Brownie -
Fresh chocolate brownie topped with chocolate sauce and ice cream was a perfect end.

BEVERAGES~
Love Dream.
Malta Basil.
Both the drinks tasted good and went well with the food.

So our meal at Agent Jack’s Bar Fun Republic was a good dining experience as the vibe of the restaurant due to live music and the food was great. Starting with a protein bowl, this bowl came with Quinoa, edamame, tofu, greens, sprouts and almonds with a Dijon apple cider vinaigrette. Loved it. Was fresh, perfect amalgamation of texture. Would have loved it more if it had more Dijon and a little more seasoning. But a healthy bowl indeed.

Then tried the watermelon feta salad. It was well balanced. Juicy sweet watermelon, salty feta, balsamic and crunchy nuts. Perfect.

Avocado toast.. just how I like it .. loaded with avocado. Some chilli flakes. I don't like my Avocado over seasoned cause it destroys the avocados natural flavor. This was perfect.

Brie and fig crostini... Sweet figs and gooey brie.. a good combination. It was tad bit sweet for me.. a little salty ingredient would balance it.

Phyllo Mushrooms with balsamic drizzle, these were delicious. The pastry was super crunchy and perfect. The mushrooms were flavorful. Loved it.

Burrata Pizza.. thin crust, delicious pizza.. however the quantity of burrata was too less.

Cottage cheese steak with tomato stew and herb rice.. the cottage cheese was fresh and soft..but needed a little more seasoning. The herb rice could have been a little more flavorful. The stew was delicious. Overall a little bland for me. Could taste only the tomatoes.

Bitter Sweet chocolate slab... This was one of the best dessert I've had in a long time. Perfect harmony of bitter and sweet chocolate ganache. Loved it.

Mango Boots – A rich and creamy mango-based drink that was both refreshing and indulgent.

["{guided_block={}, time_line=a month ago, review=We opted for buffet here and The primary positive point of our visit was the impressive variety and quality of the dishes offered on the buffet and the ambience. The kitchen staff clearly puts effort into preparation, offering a delightful mix of cuisines.

The Cheese Nuggets were a hit—crispy on the outside and warm/gooey inside. The Manchurian Dry was well-balanced and flavorful. Also, The inclusion of diverse items like Pasta, Khowswey, and various Dumplings was a pleasant surprise and added great value to the buffet. The taste of these dishes was genuinely good. The few Indian dishes available were noted for being flavorful and well-spiced, demonstrating skill across different culinary styles. Had the dining environment matched the quality of the food, this would have been a five-star review and a location we would frequent.

But, there are Major Cleanliness and Hygiene Failure
Unfortunately, the entire experience was severely compromised by unacceptable issues with cleanliness and hygiene in the dining and buffet area. The most critical issue was the pervasive presence of flies actively buzzing around and settling on the open food in the buffet line. This is a severe health and safety risk. Due to the sight of pests, we were forced to avoid several dishes entirely, including many we were looking forward to trying. This lack of sanitation completely overshadowed the good food, making the meal stressful and unappetizing. A buffet setup requires rigorous and constant attention to hygiene. They were almost closing, but still accommodated us, which I really appreciated.

The vibe is outstanding — luxurious yet calming and homely at the same time. Lots of plants, beautiful artwork, and plenty of seating. Loved the ambience from the moment I walked in.

Starters

We ordered Lamb Chops, Ceylon Black Pork, and Chicken Tokku Masala.
•	Ceylon Black Pork completely stole the show — soft, flavourful, and absolutely delicious.
•	Chicken Tokku Masala came second.
•	Surprisingly, my usual favourite Lamb Chops ranked third this time, though still good.

The Sampler Experience

While deciding on curries, we were unsure what to order. The staff brought us a sampler of different curries and rices, and the waiter explained each item patiently. This was genuinely an amazing experience and helped us choose perfectly.

Mains

We went with:
•	Prawn Yellow Coconut Curry
•	Mutton Kolumbu Curry

Both were good, but the Prawn Yellow Coconut Curry was OUT OF THIS WORLD — easily the best dish of the entire meal. It was finger-licking good.
It tasted amazing with both Malabar Parotta and Appam, but we loved it so much that we ordered plain rice — and that combination was heaven on a plate.

The Mutton Kolumbu paired really well with parotta.

Next, we ordered the Boneless Mutton Biryani. This was a pulao-style biryani (not dum), and I actually loved it. Soft mutton, beautifully spiced rice, and super flavourful.

To finish, we ordered Rasam, served hot with papad. It was the perfect conclusion to an already amazing meal.

We tried the Marinara Pizza, topped with cherry tomatoes, sun-dried tomatoes, paprika, and garlic. That said when it came to service there were a few highs and lows which I believe alters the overall experience but more on that later.

Arancini, crispy fried and served on a base of really great sauce which balanced the richness of arancini with just enough tart flavour.

We should have be warned right after entering: no friendly hello from the staff and worst 90s pop songs played way too lout from a DJ (btw: who needs a DJ for that most mainstream unpersonal song selection?).

The interior design is kind of post modern Art Deco but far from being cozy or cool.
*But now for the drinks.*:
One of the reviewers praised them for the story that would be behind each of the signature drinks.
Well, the bar menu mentions a story for each signature drink. But there is no recognisable connection between the story and the drink.
And there is not even necessarily a connection between drink description and drink. Or would you expect a garden salad with plenty of cucumber seeds that fills one third of your glass when only white rum, vodka, lime and syrup are mentioned in the menu? And
One could overlook this, if the two signature drinks we had, would have convinced by creativity and taste. But they didn’t, not at all.
The best signature drinks become classics some day. A good signature drink makes you remember drink and location. These unbalanced drinks we won’t remember.

When I finally stopped by, I was genuinely impressed with the interior and rooftop section. It has a cozy, laid-back vibe that’s rare to find in a highway-side bar. The ambiance feels just right for a casual drink or quick hangout, especially in the evenings.

But unfortunately, that’s where the positives ended for me.

The food and service were a big letdown. I ordered chicken lollipop, but the head waiter kept insisting I try the tandoor version instead. When I clearly told him I wasn’t interested and that I’d rather skip it if the regular lollipop wasn’t available, he suddenly said, “We do have the lollipop.” It felt very manipulative and pushy.

A similar thing happened with the veg starters. We ordered mushroom, but they brought paneer instead—and again, the waiter tried hard to convince us to just go with it. When we refused, he said mushroom would take 20 minutes. We agreed to wait, but then suddenly he claimed they were out of mushrooms altogether. This kind of flip-flop and forceful attitude really ruined the experience.

Food quality was average at best, and the overall attitude of the staff made it feel like they were more interested in pushing what’s convenient for them than giving the customer what they want.

In summary: Beautiful setting, poor service. Will I return? Sunday evening at this place and it was absolutely sorted. Place with very good vibes and delicious food. It was lively and packed on Sunday night too.!

Talking about ambience! Place is themed using amazing old is gold concept.! That wooden entrance really gives a feeling of it being so old.! Indoor was with Amazing wall arts, mini bar counter, more peaceful with soft music.! Out seating is amazing and very lively, very comfortable table seating with dimmed lights and a vertical garden in the corners.! Outdoor seating area is very large compared to the indoor one! Overall I found it to be very comfortable and soothing place.

Staff and service! Service was absolutely speedy and we just loved the timely availability of appetizers with our drinks and other things like cleanliness etc.! Staff was very polite and welcoming, Mr. Brendon was taking care of our table and he really did his job perfectly. I must say excellent and well trained staff.!

Dishes & Drinks, place offers amazing deals on booze. They do serve some lip smacking starters and I just falled in love with paneer makhni gravy.! We could try lot of food stuffs accompanied with refreshing drinks, everything was super delicious.

Aloo channa chat: this special salad was simply amazing. Boiled black chickpeas, deep fried squared potato pieces tossed with bell pepper, raw mango and tomatoes.! It really tasted different than a regular salad and definitely a good choice to accompany drinks.!
*** Highly recommended ***

Bombay Vadapav: deep fried meshed potato pattice served with fresh pav, chili mint dip, freshly cut onions, green chillies and garlic powder. It really gives a feeling of street food and was delectable.!

Pav bhaji sandwich: Mumbais famous dishes pav bhaji and sandwich clubbed to form this one.! It was very buttery, sandwich was grilled perfectly.! Bhaji tasted spicy and had a good texture too.! Was served along with fries.

Other appetizers like Garlic mushrooms, which was fresh mushrooms Sliced and tossed with finely chopped garlic was lip smacking. Paneer chilli, fresh paneer tossed in spicy sauces with exotic bell peppers, was upto the mark.
We could also try their chilli cheese toast! This one was baked to perfection with proper amount of cheese and chillies, served with ketchup! Good option to accompany chilled beer.!

Some refreshing and few alcoholic drinks that we could try at this place really delighted us and gave a good high.

Strawberry & pink Guava: real guava crush with strawberry syrup, topped with canned juices, taste was good and combination was little tangy.!

Tyrewala : wow this vodka based drink was very smooth, refreshing and amazing. Just loved the texture, topped with real ornage slices this drink is must try. Sweet and tangy, really went down smooth and gave a sweet high.!

We had a table reservation for 9:45 PM and arrived by 9:55 PM. Despite being just 10 minutes late, we were made to wait another 10 minutes before being seated—even though we could clearly see 4–5 empty tables inside. This initial delay set the tone for what turned out to be an underwhelming evening.

Once seated, we weren’t provided with menus until we asked for them. After deciding on our soups and starters, no server approached us for over 10 minutes, prompting me to personally request someone to take our order. There was no water on the table, and even after requesting it, the server simply forgot—walking past our table multiple times to serve others. Eventually, I had to approach someone who seemed to be the manager, only to be told, repeatedly, that “the staff is busy” and we needed to “co-operate.” Frankly, it doesn’t take much effort to bring menus, take an order, or serve water—basic expectations at any restaurant.

As for the food:

Soups: The Manchow soup was lukewarm and seemed like it came straight from the buffet, with soggy fried noodles on the side. The Tomato soup, on the other hand, had a nice basil flavor and was decent.

Starters: The Paneer Chilly was flavorful and enjoyable. Among the non-veg options, the Korean Fried Chicken had an odd fishy smell, although the sauce was good. The Pan Fried Chicken Momos were tasty, though the accompanying dip was overly sweet.

Main Course: The Chicken Tikka Masala and assorted breads were well-prepared and satisfying. However, the Chicken Biryani was disappointing—bland and lacking any real depth of flavor. The vegetarian mains—Vegetable Stir Fry in Hot Garlic Sauce and Pink Pasta—were good but took an unusually long time to arrive.

Mocktails: We tried the No-jito, a twist on the classic mojito, which didn’t stand out, and the Guava Mary, which was refreshing and enjoyable.

No desserts were ordered, mainly because by the end of the meal, our patience was running thin.

Overall, the dining experience was marred by disorganized service, inattentive staff, and inconsistent food quality. While a few dishes did manage to impress, they weren’t enough to outweigh the frustrating delays and lack of basic hospitality. For a restaurant that seems to take pride in its offerings, the service fell severely short.

A restaurant called, Suyog

Very calm & quiet place

We have been here before.

Fully AC, valet parking service available. Bar is also there.

Suyog is 30/ 35 years old restaurant.

The first dish I tried was Aloo Nazakat. This is a small appetizer with a good burst of flavors. It’s a small potato cut in half which is marinated with a spicy marination. Then it is topped with cheeses later baked in grill. I liked this dish mainly because of it size. I would say its like a small boom of flavors. The Next dish was the Falafal Pocket. This is a middle eastern dish which is prepared very nicely by the restaurant. My fourth visit to this French / Mediterranean restaurant was filled with fantastic delights, crafted dishes, amazing interactions, and sweet surprises throughout the dinner.

We were warmly welcomed at the restaurant by head chef, Mr Minocha, who named a few specialities and why they deserved consideration, and wow! -- all of them were outstanding; more on that, later. In a few minutes of our arrival, we were served complimentary kiwi mocktails, which had a high-powered soda and were mildly sweet; it didn't take long for the team to catch our taste buds for mocktails. We ordered a blueberry-based mocktail and a mango lassi, and both were authentic. The former was reasonably sweet with a significant amount of fruit % made with medium-power soda, whilst the latter had a rich % of alphonso mango [ and not concentrate ] content, unlike other same-level places where mango lassi is likely to have more of concentrate and yoghurt %.

Till the time the main course was getting ready, we were served a small plate -- Avvolto Avocado -- which was a small, soft roll containing mashed avocado with a dash of jalapeno flavour. In Pizzas, we were recommended Truffle tartufo, and gosh! The smell has started doing the talking and managed to dominate our sensations. The arugula was a skosh scratchy on the tongue, but that could easily be kept aside without affecting the taste of the pizza; it could not supersede the rich parmesan spread on the crispy layers. Next came the soups, and the chef had to do some convincing; I ain't someone who has much liking for soups. But the chef had won here; his nice smile had words written all over it. If the aroma wouldn't be all over one, then just a sip would send one in an Elysian mood. The porcini cream soup with its truffle foam, which looked like a cappuccino, was creamy and so delicious that I could keep having it.

And now came the main course -- Pan-seared Chilean Sea Bass and Lobster. The former was arguably the best I have had hitherto; A medium-sized portion served with sauteed veggies and mashed potatoes alongside, it was perfectly cooked and easy to slice that I couldn't help but scoff it quickly. If one weren't to mince for words, no words would really describe the taste; one would have to nosh it to feel it. Meanwhile, we ordered a cranberry-based mocktail, and as per our instructions, it was mildly sweet with medium-power soda; this was notable given that mocktails which are significantly or entirely cranberry-based cannot be kept away from high sweetness. And this was just another example of scrupulousness from the restaurant.

In the desserts, we were treated to a De-constructed Tiramisu, a famous Italian dish. Having a different presentation and girded by lady fingers and creme and chocolate cuts on top, it had a rich coffee texture and was brownish and spongier than the ones I have had in same-level restaurants. The size was small. The Classical-flavoured Cannoli with three flavours was a roll filled with flavoured, reasonably sweet creme, albeit one of the flavours was insipid, and possibly a change of flavours would find more takers. The chef agreed to my request to replace the original ice cream, and the chocolate ice cream [ sans almonds ] was delicious and made up for the cannolis. The size was large overall. Another off-the-menu dessert, whose name I have forgotten, which was offered to us, too, was a chocolate-based dessert whose layer was artistically molten by liquid chocolate to form a crater. It was delightful too.

Throughout our dinner, Mr Lopes and his teammates were around to ensure that our requirements were looked after, and satisfyingly so, and we were given notable suggestions from time to time; we enjoyed our chat with everyone, in particular, Mr Lopes. It was also nice to catch up with Mr Minocha earlier. I would also like to thank Mr Srinivas for personally looking into the reservation. 📍 Location & Ambiance
Nock Nock Resto Bar is located in an upscale part of Kalyan, inside Tharwani Vedant Palacia on Vasant Valley Road near D-Mart. The surroundings are surprisingly premium, with well-crafted statues and a high-end architectural feel—something you’d expect in Powai’s Hiranandani rather than Kalyan.

Once inside, the ambiance is pure “mafia boss” vibes. The dark wood interiors, green upholstered chairs, and round tables make you feel like you’re in a high-stakes meeting. The decor is eccentric yet classy, with framed pictures of animals like dogs and lions dressed in blazers, giving a Russian-mafia-meets-gentleman’s-club aesthetic.

🍽️ Dining Experience
We opted for Zomato Dining, which helped us save ₹400 on our total bill of ₹3,000. Ordering food one by one worked well, allowing us to pace the meal and enjoy every bite. The food quality was excellent, with generous portions.

🔹 Food Ordered:
•	Signature Dishes (Detailed pricing wasn’t noted but falls in the ₹400-₹600 range per dish)
•	Drinks: LIT (Long Island Iced Tea) – A strong mix of whiskey, vodka, and rum, giving a solid kick
•	Beer – On the expensive side, so not highly recommended

🍷 Pricing & Offers
The alcohol pricing is steep, so if you’re planning to drink, be mindful of the cost. However, with Zomato Dining, we got a discount, making it a better deal.

👨‍🍳 Service
The service was excellent—staff was attentive yet non-intrusive. They let us enjoy our meal without unnecessary interruptions. For a birthday celebration, they accommodated our request to bring in our own cake and made sure everything went smoothly.

🔍 Final Verdict
✔ Ambiance: 5/5 – Mafia-style interiors with a premium touch
✔ Food: 4.5/5 – Great quality, good portions
✔ Drinks: 3.5/5 – Pricey but well-made
✔ Service: 5/5 – Professional and efficient
✔ Overall Experience: 4.5/5

Would I recommend it?
Yes, especially for those looking for a unique dining experience in Kalyan. It’s expensive but worth it for the ambiance and service. ["{guided_block={}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=BEAUTIFUL ESCAPE to clam down, to relax, to enjoy the elegant atmosphere and the food.

From the location aspect one of the best places in Mumbai. You can even sit outside on a terrace and enjoy the view over Powai lake.

We tried the Sunday Brunch which was really good. The focus of the buffet is Indiean Cuisine but yes you find some pasta dishes, sushi, momos, dim sums and fresh seasonal salads. For all dessert and sweet teeth this is the place for you. This place offers one of the biggest dessert varieties I experienced in Mumbai. Amazing.

We were there at 12:30 and this is a great time as it's not crowded and all is fresh cooked.

The stuff is friendly and they try to assist you with everything. They even guide you along the buffet and explain the dishes.

Prices are on the high side. Buffet plus two bottles of water 2 person EUR 105,--

Out of all the experiences it's a great location and if you like Indian Food it's a great choice but I personally have visited places with more vegan, glutenfree options.

This restaurant of Westin hotel ,Powai is located on the bank of Powai lake & what an amazing view all around... i simply loved it.., name_person=Juhi Sarkar}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=5 months ago, review=Lake view Cafe at The Westin truly lives up to its reputation as my favorite spot in the city! The location is absolutely stunning, offering a serene and destressing ambiance that's hard to beat. It's definitely a must-visit for anyone looking for a peaceful escape.
The food is undeniably good, and the staff are absolutely great – always attentive and friendly. However, there's certainly room for improvement when it comes to variety.
To enhance the buffet experience, I strongly recommend adding beverages to the buffet selection. Including options like sparkling water, tea, and coffee would be a fantastic enhancement. Additionally, it would be incredibly helpful to have the menu on the table so guests can browse offerings before heading to the buffet. Everyone was singing and dancing, and they even had screen showing the ICC World Cup match, which made it even more lively.

Service was quite quick initially. We ordered masala peanuts- nicely done with boiled peanuts and onion-tomato salad, The chicken pops were good too, not like the KFC-style cornflake coating but bread crumb–crusted, crispy, and tasty. The meat-loaded pizza was great - thin crust, well-balanced toppings with sausages, chicken pieces, and the right amount of cheese that didn’t overpower the flavor.

Do check it out!, name_person=1TeaspoonLove}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Pot_Rice], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=9 months ago, review=Sampan delivers an authentic Asian dining experience with a well-curated menu and a vibrant ambiance. The décor, lighting, and setup reflect the essence of an upscale Asian restaurant, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere.

Food Highlights
1. Kung Pao Potato – Crispy potato cubes tossed in a flavorful, spicy-sweet sauce with crunchy peanuts and dried chilies, offering a satisfying bite.

2. Salt and Pepper Fish – Lightly battered fish fillets, stir-fried with salt, crushed pepper, and subtle spices, delivering a crispy yet tender texture.

3. Crunchy Lotus Stem – Thinly sliced lotus stems fried to perfection, coated in a tangy and slightly sweet glaze, making for an addictive appetizer.

4. Shanghai Chicken – Succulent chicken pieces cooked in a rich, umami-packed Shanghai-style sauce with a balanced hint of spice.

5. Crunchy Garlic Prawns – Medium sized prawns fried to a golden crisp and infused with a bold garlic flavor, enhancing their natural sweetness.

6. Fish and Prawns Fried Rice – Fragrant, well-seasoned fried rice generously loaded with mushrooms, fish and prawns, offering a hearty and flavorful main course.

7. Caramel Custard – A silky-smooth custard with a perfectly caramelized top, delivering a rich and creamy finish. Caramel was a bit bitter though.

8. Ice Cream with Litchi – A refreshing dessert where the creaminess of the ice cream complements the juicy sweetness of litchis. Canned litchies were served. Fresh litchies would taste even better.

Ambiance: Authentic Asian-themed with a cozy yet upscale feel.

Service: Professional and attentive staff, providing prompt service and answering queries efficiently.

Food Quantity: Portions were adequate and well-balanced.

Cleanliness & Hygiene: Well-maintained and hygienic dining space.

Impressed with its flavorful dishes, well-managed service, and immersive ambiance.

The Margherita Pizza at Indigo Deli was a masterclass in simplicity. The crust was paper-thin, with a delicate crunch that gave way to a soft, airy interior. Ambiance: Convenient Food Court Setting

As part of the Nine Dine food court, Indigo Deli offers a convenient and casual dining experience. The food court is well-maintained and clean, with ample seating and a lively atmosphere.

Service: Friendly and Efficient

The service at Indigo Deli was friendly and efficient, with the staff happy to answer our questions about the menu and make recommendations. Our order was prepared quickly, and we were impressed by the speed and accuracy of the service.

Indigo Deli is a must-visit destination for anyone craving authentic and delicious European-inspired cuisine. The Margherita Pizza is a standout dish, and I'm excited to try more of their offerings in the future.

The menu boasts a variety of food options, including breakfast platters, which might initially seem impressive. However, the taste of the food is compromised and does not justify the high prices. For a cafe that markets itself as a premium experience, the quality of the dishes leaves much to be desired.

Ambience and Seating

The sitting space is one of the better aspects of Cafe Trofima. Considering it is a cafe, the seating is comfortable and suitable for casual conversations or work. However, the overall ambience is just average, with no music to elevate the vibe. It lacks the warmth or charm that many would expect from a cafe in this area.

Service

The service is satisfactory but nothing extraordinary. While the staff is polite and attends to customers in a timely manner, the overall experience doesn’t stand out as memorable.

Location and Accessibility

A significant downside is the lack of parking space, which can be a hassle, especially given the busy location of Shivaji Park. Visitors arriving in their own vehicles may find it inconvenient.

Pricing

The prices are on the higher side, making it hard to justify for the quality of food and overall experience provided. While there are plenty of food options to choose from, the value for money is not reflected in the offerings.

Verdict

Cafe Trofima is overrated and doesn’t quite live up to its reputation. While it has some redeeming qualities like decent seating and satisfactory service, the compromised food taste, lack of parking, and high prices make it hard to recommend wholeheartedly. It could work as a one-time visit for those curious about its breakfast platters, but better options are available in and around the area for a more satisfying experience.

Located on the 2nd floor of The Hub Mall, Western Express Highway, this Restaurant delivers a solid spread of veg & non-veg unlimited food in a comfortable, spacious setting.

From the moment we arrived, the ambience hit the right note — generous seating, warm lighting, and a relaxed vibe that works for both family dinners and friendly meet-ups. The staff are attentive and the buffet layout is well organised. They allow you to enjoy your dinner without disturbing much but be available when you call out any of them.

On to the food — you’ll find a wide variety of dishes: live counters with pani puri, soups, a full spread of starters (veg & non-veg kebabs, tandoori items), main courses ranging from North Indian to Chinese & Mughlai, breads, rice, and a nice dessert section.

Key favourites: the paneer tikka, chicken rarhya, lasooni fish, and for desserts the dudhi halw and kheer are worth a try.

With the special offer of ₹499 on Mondays & Tuesdays, you’re looking at an exceptional deal for the area.

The location is convenient for the Western Suburbs (Goregaon East), making it a solid choice for buffet restaurant in that region.

If I were to offer some tips:

Go early (lunch/dinner) to avoid peak crowd and ensure you get the full buffet spread without items running out.

Try out your best veg and non veg dishes - one at a time so that you don't get confused.
Start with the live counters (pani puri, kebabs) and work your way to mains & desserts — being strategic helps when you want to make the most of a buffet.

Bring your foodie group or family — the place has big seating which is great for group bookings.

In short: if you’re in Mumbai’s Western Suburbs and on the lookout for an unlimited food buffet restaurant that is within your budget, this is very much worth a visit. Luft the Air in Veera Desai offers a genuinely enjoyable experience, striking a great balance between ambience and food. The venue is smartly designed with two distinct areas. a relaxed dining space perfect for a proper meal, and a vibrant club area ideal for drinks and later-evening energy. This dual concept works well, catering to different moods seamlessly.

The ambience in both sections is well-executed. The dining area provides a comfortable and inviting atmosphere for conversation and enjoying food, while the club side has a more upbeat vibe. The overall aesthetic feels modern and stylish.

Now, for the food – it was definitely a highlight! We sampled:

*   Tuscan Chicken Roulade Tikka: A creative fusion dish. The chicken was succulent, well-spiced (true to the 'tikka' promise), and the Tuscan-inspired elements added a unique, delicious twist. Very enjoyable.
*   Grilled Chicken Pandhra Rassa: This Maharashtrian classic was executed beautifully. The Pandhra Rassa (white curry) was rich, creamy, and flavourful, perfectly complementing the tender grilled chicken. A comforting yet sophisticated dish.
*   Churros Palate: A delightful end to the meal. The churros were crispy on the outside, fluffy inside, and served with delectable accompaniments. A satisfying and fun dessert.
Special Thanks to Anup for serving the delicious food.

Overall, our experience at Luft the Air was very positive. The service was attentive, the distinct spaces offered flexibility for our evening, and the food quality was consistently good across the dishes we tried. We truly enjoyed the flavours and the atmosphere.

In short: Luft the Air delivers on both food and vibe. It's a great spot for a dinner where you might want to transition into a more lively setting later, or simply enjoy a quality meal in the dedicated dining area. The political influence surrounding this place is obvious \u2014 and when powerful people are involved, the public\u2019s peace and rights are ignored. It have both ac and out side area. They have the open area but the best part of that area is it's open but it has big air conditioner there. So in this hit summers u can still enjoy the out side area. As the inside ac area is little dark which creates a different ambiance which is very soothing. The food here is amazing value for money. It’s my go-to bar and my go-to place. Dailys  completely defines the Bandra chilling scene — it has that effortless vibe that keeps pulling you back.

This spot has been around for quite some time, and every visit has been a consistently good experience. They’ve got a great music scene (especially their weekend techno nights), fantastic brunches, good drinks, delicious food, and a genuinely warm, attentive team.

One thing I really appreciate is how they keep updating the ambience every few months. Somehow, it always works — it feels fresh without losing the familiar comfort.

I recommend Dailies to anyone visiting Bandra.
